 Makueni County has launched a campaign to grow 200,000 tree seedlings during the October-November-December (OND) rainy season, as part of its long-term ambition to plant 34 million trees by 2032.
 Deputy Governor Lucy Mulili launched the campaign at Ngwata CTTI in Kambu on Thursday, where 20,000 seedlings were distributed to community members for planting on their farms.
 Mulili said the county has made significant progress in increasing its tree cover from 5 per cent in 2021 to 8 per cent in 2026, while forest cover has risen from 12 per cent to 14 per cent through the enhanced tree-growing initiative.
 To curb illegal tree felling, she said the County Government is working closely with the Kenya Forest Service to ensure that only licensed persons are authorised to harvest and utilise forest resources in accordance with the law.
 November 20, 2026
